beliefs: f(0)=472.73 is a single isolated spike, not an interval; nearby values are smooth [E1, E2]
For x>0, f(x) is negative and grows in magnitude roughly like -C*x^p with p~3.85 for x>=2 [E1, E8]
For 0<x<1, f(x) is negative, smooth, slowly varying from about -36.8 near 0+ to -41.7 at x=1 [E1, E2, E3]
For -1<x<0, f(x) is negative, smooth, slowly varying from about -11.7 near 0- to -7.4 at x=-1 [E1, E2, E3]
On the positive side, f dips sharply just past x=1 (to about -53 at x=1.5) then rejoins the power law by x~2.5 [E4]
On the negative side, f rises steeply in magnitude just past x=-1 (to about -3.2 at x=-1.5) then rejoins the power law by x~2.5 [E4]
For x<0 the magnitude grows smoothly through |x|~93.3 (reaching ~8.85e7) then drops sharply to a plateau of -2.497e7 by |x|=93.6 [E6, E7, E9]
The negative-side cliff is between |x|=93.3 and |x|=93.6, not between 91 and 94 [E9]
The negative-side plateau at -2.497e7 holds from |x|~93.6 out to |x|=128 [E6, E7, E9]
The negative-side power law with exponent ~4.37 fits |x|=2.5 to ~60 reasonably but drifts, so a smooth interpolation through observed negative-side anchors is used for |x|>=2.5 [E5, E6]
The positive side shows no cliff/plateau; it continues the power law cleanly through x=128 [E8]
The positive-side power law constant is slightly higher than 2.54 (E8 shows ~-2.54*x^3.85 underestimates at large x) [E8]
notes: Moved the negative-side cliff from |x|~91-94 to |x|~93.3-93.6 based on E9 (magnitude keeps growing to ~8.85e7 at 93.3, then snaps to plateau at 93.6). Also refined positive-side power law constant to better fit E8's large-x values.
